dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you're here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anything interesting you wanna talk about today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Morning! Are we going out for some tasty food today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's ready to go anytime!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Nighty night, {NICKNAME}, and sweet dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And don't you worry, Paimon'll be with you all the way!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About riches...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon... doesn't feel so good...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon hasn't opened a treasure chest in so long. If this keeps up...

choices.text: If this keeps up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Paimon floats, so that'll never work.

choices.text: You'll get caught in a hunting trap with a one-Mora bait someday.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About cat people and dog people...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Which do you like more, cats or dogs?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I prefer Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Um, that... That's cheating...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no! Paimon's not a pet!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Language

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You learn new things so quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've already got such a good grasp of Teyvat's language.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're a good teacher, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe...

choices.text: Who knows?
Maybe the quality of your nasty nicknames will improve, someday.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About rock, paper, scissors...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should get something to eat! Aw, but Paimon doesn't wanna go over there...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shall we decide with a game of rock-paper-scissors, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, okay!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Alright then. Rock, paper—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: —Super Paimon Tornado!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the luck of the draw...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Urrrrgh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm? Are there pigeons around?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, Paimon's just hungry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What Paimon needs right now is a traveler who can whip up some delicious Sticky Honey Roast.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, who's going to be the lucky traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Cider Lake...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cider Lake never freezes, no matter what time of the year it is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The best apple ciders in Mondstadt can only be made using the fresh water from this lake.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It really does taste great! Paimon could drink two big bottles in a second!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tee-hee!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: With your size...

choices.text: I can't believe that you can drink that much water...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon always has room for tasty drinks.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh...

choices.text: I guess the world really is a big place.
So many things to consider...
...And not explode like an Anemo Slime.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Razor

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you heard of the brush?

choices.text: You mean pens made using animal hair...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's correct! They say that finely-made brushes sell for high prices among Liyue's merchants!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, would you like to make some too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh! But the wild wolves are too fierce, so we should use Razor's fur to make brushes instead!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Razor's fur is all downy and soft. It'll definitely make great wolf pens! We could make lots of Mora like this!

choices.text: Brushes made like that would conduct electricity.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Besides, Razor isn't a wolf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Why are they called wolf pens, then?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, does Cider Lake look like it's full of cider to you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. You have a point.

choices.text: I'm not sure we could use them...
...For writing purposes?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Benny's Adventure Team

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you want to adventure together with Benny's Adventure Team, you have to come prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Domains are very dangerous, so you should always take care to double and triple check your supplies in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's heard that the Adventurers' Guild has compiled a list of four hundred and sixty-three different ways of dying in these domains...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Bennett got you killed by accident, Paimon and Bennett would never forgive ourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Why am I the only one dying here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's because according to the numbers, Paimon can avoid three hundred and twenty-two causes of death just by floating!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I suddenly don't feel like exploring these domains...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the "Wondermaid"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's time for Paimon's Little Life Tips!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Little Life Tips?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In Mondstadt, if there's something you can't fix, or something that you can't get clean, no matter what you do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you ever run into something you can't handle yourself, you just need to shout this name to the skies:

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Noeeeelle!"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And everything that's troubling you will be swept away in an instant.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So this is one of the tricks to living in Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pretty impressive...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Kaeya and Diluc

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Diluc and Kaeya are really alike, so why don't they get along?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are they alike, again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Kaeya's the kind of guy who acts shady in the light of day...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: While Diluc is a shining beacon of justice in the dark of night!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't you think that's kinda the same thing...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uhh... I still don't see it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Effort and Reward

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon finds that hard work hardly works here in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why'd you say so?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just look at Huffman from the Knights of Favonius. He does his best at his duties every day...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the ever-relaxed Captain Kaeya is his boss.

choices.text: Hmm, but isn't Jean, who works the hardest...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Well, how about this, then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Venti's the god of Mondstadt, and he's the laziest of them all!

choices.text: ...The Acting Grand Master?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Dihua Marsh

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you know? The reeds in Dihua Marsh are common materials used in making paper.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The solid reed cores are used to make pens, while the hollow part is used to make flutes, and it's considered an elegant art in Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over the years, many heroes and swordmen have also chosen Dihua Marsh as the location of their duels.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The more reeds, the more elegant the place. But in places where the reeds are the thickest, the water can be quite deep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So there are lots of unlucky duelists who fall in and drown while the duel is on...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And what's my takeaway from this supposed to be?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't fight!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Couplets

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's heard that couplets are a traditional art form in Liyue. If you can write a line that works as a second half to one that someone else has written, you'll be well paid!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But linking the couplet is hard, so it's not easy money.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not only does the rhythm need to match, but the meaning has to as well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm, care to give an example?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... "Windrise's winds never churn."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Um, "But the Sea of Clouds' clouds always return."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Not bad!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's not waste time here. We've got some money to make!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Heart's Desire

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Walk in seven clockwise circles, then walk in seven anticlockwise circles, then open your eyes...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you sleepwalking?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope! Paimon is just trying to see if that antique shop from "Heart's Desire" actually exists!

choices.text: Well, assuming that a shop in a story does exist...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A Slime Creator!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Does such a thing even exist?

choices.text: What would you like to buy, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Beidou

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How do you become as popular and cool as Captain Beidou?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: With enough experience...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's already seen lots of things from adventuring together with you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: One also needs to experience trials and setbacks...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon almost drowned that one time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Maintain an inspirational disposition...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-huh! Paimon's always rooted for you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: One must also have a mature outlook towards problems...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Are you just trying to say that Paimon can't make it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Ningguang

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How does a person become as rich, or as rich, or as super rich as Lady Ningguang?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that the only impression she gives you? Riches?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, there's the huge Jade Chamber, too! But isn't that also made of Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, you need an excellent mind...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's really good at giving people nicknames!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You need to be very familiar with the workings of the markets...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A serving of Fisherman's Toast goes for 1025 Mora, and no discounts even on rainy days.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You also require exceptional workmanship...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... how do you make friends with a really rich person?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, you're giving up already?!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Qiqi Being a Zombie

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think that Qiqi... needs to drink blood?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's not a zombie, Paimon, that's a vampire.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, will her arms fall off suddenly?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's also not a zombie, that's a ghoul.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: uh. As expected of a traveler. You really know a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what special thing can zombies do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Exercises?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes a lot of sense! So zombies are the ones that can perform exercises!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Vision Hunt Decree

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's hard to talk about the recent events in Inazuma and not mention the Vision Hunt Decree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you don't have a Vision, so you don't have to worry about losing one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #On the flip side, if you are caught by the Tenryou Commission, {NICKNAME}, you also can't surrender your Vision in exchange for your life...

choices.text: I can tell them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Another reason to have Paimon around... Wait, WHAT!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I wouldn't let them take you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's more like it.

choices.text: We'd just go to jail...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... W—Well, if that's how it would go down, then maybe you should hand Paimon over to them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait a minute! How about we just don't get caught in the first place?

choices.text: And suffer punishment together...
...That you are my Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Gorou

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you mulling over, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you remember Gorou's fluffy ears?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon really wants something like that... Or maybe horns similar to the ones Ganyu has. Ganyu's horns are pretty cute as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you have any ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me see, hmm... Oh, I found something!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Really? Aw, {NICKNAME}, Paimon always knew you were reliable!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ta-da! I present to you the Tusk of Monoceros Caeli!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't need that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* If Paimon can't have Gorou's fluffy ears, then maybe at least something like his fluffy tail...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bubadada! Here you go — Tail of Boreas!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Not that! Also, combining those two is definitely not the look Paimon is going for!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Kamisato Ayaka

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, you look so serious today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's because Paimon's thinking about serious things.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's jealous of people from wealthy and influential families. They have an endless supply of Mora and mountains of delicious food to eat...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't disagree. Those are exactly the things you're fond of.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But after getting to know Ayaka better, Paimon realized that a young lady from a noble family can also have her share of hardships.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She needs to shoulder her clan's duties and responsibilities. She works so hard and has very little time for herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayaka must be exhausted, she should try to relax a bit...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, that's right! Let's invite Ayaka to the next festival!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If she got an invite from us, there's no way she'd refuse.

choices.text: Yeah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, if Ayaka's around, she can pick up the tab for us...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I should've seen that coming...

choices.text: I'd like to go to another festival with her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Festival Traditions

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's a well-established tradition that during Inazuman celebrations everyone's wearing festive masks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon tried to look around the stalls, but hasn't found any mask that fits...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you really want a mask of your own?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Not wearing a mask during an Inazuman festival is the same as not receiving a bouquet at the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me make one for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whoa! {NICKNAME}, you're the best!

choices.text: Hmmm, I wonder what kind of mask will fit you best?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, Paimon Slime!

choices.text: How about... a slime mask?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Yoimiya

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think Yoimiya's dad's poor hearing is related to fireworks?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's been making and testing fireworks for many years now, and being exposed to the sound of gunpowder explosions on a daily basis... Paimon can see how that might've worn down his ears...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes! Since Yoimiya is inheriting her family business, does that mean she'll have trouble hearing other people in the future, just like her dad?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon won't let that happen! Let's think of some way to help her!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you have any suggestions, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Um...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon could follow Yoimiya around and cover her ears whenever needed...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then you'd need to leave me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Without Paimon, you'd lose your guide. Paimon wouldn't leave you like that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... What should we do for Yoimiya...

choices.text: Actually...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! Paimon didn't think of that solution! You're so smart!

choices.text: Heh... That was the first thing that came to my mind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? So you knew this whole time, but didn't tell Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How could you! You bully!

choices.text: But I wanted to give you an opportunity for a mental workout.
She can simply wear earplugs while working with fireworks.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Sayu's Troubles

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sayu seems to have a lot on her mind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't understand why she'd have so many worries.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess this is what they call growing pains.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon can't relate to that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After all, it's not Paimonly to worry too much.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmmm...

choices.text: Bad news! We're almost out of Mora.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What? Noooo!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See, you're not as carefree as you thought.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How could you prank Paimon like that...

choices.text: I guess we'll have to tighten the purse strings for the next few days...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Naku Weed

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though Naku Weed has a flower-like structure, its "petals" are in fact leaves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Its actual bloom is rather fragile, so the surrounding leaves try their hardest to grow strong and protect it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, just like Paimon is protecting you right now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like you? Oh, is Naku Weed edible too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right! ...Wait? What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Swords

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, have you noticed?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In Inazuma, people who wear swords on their waists are a minority. Most soldiers use spears.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could it be that swords are a symbol of status... Should we wear them as well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the swords here are all too big for Paimon... There's no other way, we'll have to find a famous swordsmith to make a custom one!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A custom-made sword will cost a lot of Mora though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you saying that Mora is more important than the desires of your lovely companion?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Actually, I've already prepared something for you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Really? Let's have a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Isn't that the knife we use to cut fruit?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, at least it's the right size for you...

choices.text: Ahem, "What matters isn't the value of the sword..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nice try, but Paimon won't fall for this, no matter how cool it sounds!

choices.text: "It's the fighting spirit."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Canned Knowledge...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Free knowledge without having to study at all? Canned Knowledge is amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could Sumeru have Canned Knowledge about the different customs of the seven nations, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If so, Paimon could just open a can every time we get to a new place. Paimon wouldn't have to explain things ever again!

choices.text: Or we could just open them all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... but traveling wouldn't be any fun without surprises to look forward to!

choices.text: Plus, if we opened them all here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay scrap that idea! No more Canned Knowledge. Let's save our Mora for something else!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something like... Oh! Tipping Paimon for guide services! Heehee, seems fair, right?

choices.text: I wouldn't even need Paimon as a guide anymore.
Here in Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Eremites...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Eremites are a real motley crew...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's certainly a diverse range of characters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmm... yeah, that could explain it! Paimon can play lots of different characters too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Judgy Paimon, knowledgeable Paimon, helpful Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...And of course the classic, completely-misses-the-point Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Grand Bazaar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The residents of the Grand Bazaar are all so talented!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They sell their own woven goods, beautiful vases and jars, and delicious-smelling spices that make Paimon's tummy start rumbling...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And they all sing and dance really well! Paimon wishes she could do that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, if you're serious about it, there's no reason you couldn't learn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Really?

choices.text: Well for starters...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You won't trip over yourself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! Paimon always forgets how useful flying can be!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then! Let's go bust a move at the Grand Bazaar and watch everyone shower Paimon with admiration!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Aha, so that's what this is all about.

choices.text: You have a natural advantage when it comes to dancing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Divination...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: People in Sumeru seem to take divination and fortune-telling pretty seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For starters, there's astrology, although only the scholars get to practice that. But ordinary citizens have their ways, too. They can do divinations with just a cup of coffee!

choices.text: It's the nation of wisdom after all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon heard that they can tell your fate just by looking at the bottom of a finished cup of coffee...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds way easier than climbing to the top of a tower and staring at the stars all night!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you interested in learning your fate, too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... although, Paimon's really more interested in finding out what the coffee tastes like.

choices.text: It seems like people have an insatiable curiosity to learn about everything, including their own future.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Bimarstan...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, healthcare is FREE in Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you feeling unwell, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, not right now. Thanks for asking, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe... Eating the street food on every corner has never sounded so tempting!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your stomach is going to punish you for that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If so, Paimon'll go see a doctor and get treated — it's all for free! It'd be a waste not to take advantage of this, don't you think?

choices.text: Maybe... but then again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *gasp* Oh no! So no more delicious food, then?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That, plus the doctor would make you take the most bitter-tasting medicine ever.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Okay... Maybe Paimon needs to reconsider this idea...

choices.text: The treatment would likely include a restricted diet.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Scholars...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So many people in Sumeru want to become scholars.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Motivated by this ambition, they all study really hard to try and achieve it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon bets that the first ever scholar didn't set out to become a scholar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... so what do you think the first ever scholar's ambition was?

choices.text: Probably...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But isn't a scholar's ultimate goal supposed to be "pursuing the highest and greatest knowledge" or something?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's sure that it must have been because of a fervent desire for knowledge that they became Sumeru's first true scholar.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Writing papers is how you pursue knowledge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what about when it's the highest and greatest knowledge of all...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Even then, if you wanted to prove it, you'd need a research paper.

choices.text: And after that, you'd need to start working on another paper

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Okay, Paimon's got it! Come on, don't look so sad! It's not like you have to worry about writing papers yourself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Y—You've never had to write a paper before, right...?

choices.text: To validate your original thesis...
To get their research paper written as quickly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Aranara names...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arama, Arana, Araja, Arakavi... Whew, Aranara names are so hard to remember...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The only bit Paimon's sure of is that they all start with "Ara"!

choices.text: Right, so if you were an Aranara...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, and as for you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, actually, they'd probably call you "Nara Traveler"...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, we're all Nara to them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So if there was someone whose actual name was "Nara," what would the Aranara call them?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Nara Nara"... I guess. Sounds kinda cute.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, yeah.

choices.text: Your name would be "Arapaimon."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Magic...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney's magic shows are amazing! Paimon never would've guessed how he did it before he revealed his secret.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hold on... I just thought of a magic trick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You know how to do magic too?

choices.text: Yep. I can make a big magician's hat float in the air...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Really? How do you do that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hehe, simple! I put Paimon inside the hat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Why would Paimon be... Ohhh, so Paimon's the one making it float!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, in that case, Paimon has an idea for an even better magic trick!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh? What is it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Behold, the bottomless hat! No matter how many plates of delicious food you throw into it, it'll never get full!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh... Wait, so where would the plates go?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, good point! Umm... Oh, the hat spits the empty plates back out! Tada! Whaddya think?

choices.text: And even make it move at my command.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Mysterious Treasure of the Fontaine Research Institute...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: At the Fontaine Research Institute, they research clockwork and different energy sources, right? So how come there are rumors about a mystery treasure?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It'd make more sense if the treasure was owned by a bandit or a pirate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon's not sure that the researchers' and technicians' definition of "treasure" is really mysterious enough to get excited about...

choices.text: Hmm... What about "researcher by day, bandit by night"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm... Well for starters, it sounds exhausting. Imagine finishing your day job, then working a whole other job all night... When would they get time to rest?

choices.text: Maybe they wouldn't need to rest...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! A mystery treasure left by a clockwork meka who's a researcher by day and a bandit by night... Now that sounds more like it!

choices.text: If they were actually a clockwork meka in disguise!
Does that sound mysterious enough?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Fonta...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fonta tastes amazing, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yep. It's so refreshing, especially when you down the whole thing in one big gulp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can you buy a glass for Paimon? Paimon's always wanted to try that thing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What thing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just buy it, you'll see in a minute!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Glug glug glug glug...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahhhhh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's what those drunkards do after they clink their glasses together. Paimon's been itching to try it for ages!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't imitate them, Paimon... It's not a good look on you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Melusines...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Apparently, every Melusine gets their own special token when they're born. They treat it as a symbol of their very being.

choices.text: If you were a Melusine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Definitely a fork! To represent Paimon's lifelong mission to taste all the delicious food in the whole world!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not Mora, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, good point... Yeah, if it were Mora, it'd mean that Paimon's destined to be a super rich person. Then Paimon could buy anything she wants!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmmmmm... Argh, Paimon's so torn! Both are so tempting...

choices.text: How about a fork made from Mora?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that's a great idea!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, enough about Paimon. Your token would probably be... a cooking pot, to represent being Paimon's personal gourmet chef!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No no no, my token would be Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, really?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: With Paimon as my token, everything that you have would ultimately belong to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Okay sure. Friends share everything, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Haha, yeah... My stuff would still be mine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, no fair!

choices.text: Then you can have your cake and eat it, so to speak.
What would your token be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Armchair Detectives...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So apparently, some detectives in Fontaine manage to solve cases without ever setting foot outside their homes. They call them "armchair detectives"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's what they call "working from home," right? Sounds pretty cushy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, how do they figure out the truth if they never even go to the crime scene? ...Oh, Paimon knows! They must be using divination.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're thinking of fortune-tellers, Paimon. Not detectives.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... yeah...

choices.text: In any case...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean... Oh, the detective must have people collecting information for them...

choices.text: Perhaps, or...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But... that would mean the detective gets all the credit for our hard work! Bet they make a tidy sum of Mora off of it, too! Hmph, Paimon won't stand for that. Let's go have a little talk with Detective Armchair right now!

choices.text: Maybe they post commissions at the Adventurers Guild?
Surely the evidence isn't just dropping itself off at the detective's doorstep.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Resolving Conflicts...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's heard that even in Natlan, there are lots of ways to resolve conflict that don't involve contests of strength.

choices.text: Really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Like, apparently, some people in the Children of Echoes settle their disputes by holding a dance-off!

choices.text: A dance-off?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And just dance their socks off?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Until one person gets so exhausted, they can't get up anymore?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait, what the... Hold on, that IS a contest of strength!

choices.text: So like, they'll mutually decide on a time and place...
In the Nation of War?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Ways to Make a Fortune...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess what? Paimon just thought of the best Mora-making idea ever!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh? Do tell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just look how many people pass by this place every day. If we opened a business here, right outside the Stadium, we'd make a fortune without even trying!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... What would you sell?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh... maybe... alchemical potions from Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think there's already people selling similar stuff...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, ummm... Ooh! Ores from Liyue! Yeah, we could make a killing off of those!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Pretty sure the Children of Echoes are already in that business, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... Wait, Paimon's got it — rugs from Sumeru! Those'll definitely be a hit!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, that's the specialty of the Masters of the Night-Wind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well then... Then we'll fence the whole Stadium up! And charge an admission fee to everyone who tries to get inside, whether they're a contestant or a spectator!

choices.text: Pretty sure someone will take you into custody...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Grrrrrrrr! Why does getting rich have to be so hard?

choices.text: Before you finish doing that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Ways to Make Friends With Saurians...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oooh, there are so many cute Saurians in Natlan! Paimon's gonna make friends with every single one!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh? Someone sounds confident...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You bet! Paimon's got it all figured out!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh you do, huh? Come on then, what's the secret to making Saurian friends?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's really simple! First, you've gotta sweet-talk them, show 'em you mean well so they relax their defenses. Then, you gently pat them on the head — that makes them feel more comfortable around you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Last but not least: Get 'em some good grub! The way to a Saurian's heart is through the stomach, after all! What do you think? Solid plan, huh?

choices.text: Hmm, why do I get the feeling that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Would not! Paimon can't be won over by some cheap tricks!

choices.text: Huh? Oh, you misunderstand! I meant to say that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah! Flattery, really? You think that'll work on Paimon? Think again!

choices.text: But I was being sincere, Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait, really? Sweet Madame? Oh, heck yes! Paimon could totally go for some of that right now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uhh... What's with that smug look on your face? ...What!? Is Paimon missing something?

choices.text: Ah, how can I prove it you? With some Sweet Madame, perhaps?
You're as cute as a baby Saurian!
These tactics would also work really well on you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Children of Echoes' Gems...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, so the valleys here are just bursting with shiny gemstones!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't come across that kind of opportunity every day! Why don't we start a dig somewhere? If we're lucky, we might unearth something super valuable. Then we'd never have to worry about running out of Mora again!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm... But how would you actually know when you've hit the jackpot? Can you even tell which stones are the valuable ones?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, well... As long as something's bright and shiny, then it must be worth a lot, right?

choices.text: That makes us sound just like...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, except we're in Natlan now — so instead of "evil dragon," it's "noble Saurian"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #"O brave and keen {NICKNAME}, let this noble Saurian lead you to the most precious gem in the world!"

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Great! Except she can't tell which stones are the valuable ones, so how's that gonna work?

choices.text: ...evil hoarding dragons in children's fairytales!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Collective of Plenty and the Flower-Feather Clan...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's heard that everyone from the Collective of Plenty is built like a bricklayer!

choices.text: Does that mean you'll become Buffmon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No! Paimon likes herself the way she is now.

choices.text: Okay, then what about staying with the Flower-Feather Clan instead? They're adept fliers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But... isn't Paimon good enough at flying already?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, but then you'd be able to carry me when you fly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, not happening! How would that even be possible?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, if you had those muscles I talked about...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, geez, not this again... For the last time, no!

choices.text: I'm sure they could help you sharpen your skills!
...if you were to stay there awhile, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Frostmoon Scions

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon heard that the Frostmoon Scions worship the moon. So, what do you think they get up to during the daytime?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uhh... just go about their normal lives, I guess?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way, not if they're up all night worshiping! Paimon bets they have a really unusual daily routine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Unusual how?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like, uh... When the sun comes up, they probably shapeshift into huge boulders and take a nice long nap.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When night falls, they wake back up again — and with a swish and a swoosh, they're back in human form! Then, they sneak away to start getting up to their secret, mysterious work...

choices.text: So let me guess — the worst-case scenario for them is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, exactly! See, you got it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, I got it... You're getting mixed up between "Scion" and "Sayu" again.

choices.text: Blowing through nap time and doing an all-day and all-nighter?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Whiz-Kid Mechanic

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aino definitely lives up to her reputation as a whiz-kid mechanic. Everything she builds is so... creative.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She uses unlikely materials and slightly whacky designs, but all her inventions work even better than expected!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Which invention have you fallen in love with now, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The cleaner bot's pretty cool!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should get her to build one for us. It would be really handy to have in the Serenitea Pot!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Really, just the cleaner bot?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, you're right! We might as well make the most of Aino's talents. Let's get a dish-washer bot, a tidy-up bot, a gardener, and one to feed the pets...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: While we're at it, it'd be great to get a chat bot, too. That way, Tubby will have someone to talk to when we're not around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good idea. Anything else to add?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... We could get a cooking bot? Something like the supreme cuisine machine, y'know? It'd be nice to have the option, but of course, there's no substitute for your home cooking, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although, all these robots everywhere would take up a lot of space... Maybe it'd be better if we got Aino to combine them all into a single machine!

choices.text: So basically...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait, you're right... Ineffa can do all of that stuff...

choices.text: All that, and far more besides.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... You're not seriously thinking of giving Paimon's job to someone else, are you!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, no, that could never work! There's only one Ineffa, and she has to take care of Aino. We can't separate them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't get Paimon wrong, Ineffa's great, but, but... being a housekeeper in the Serenitea Pot would be too easy for her, don't you think? It'd be a real shame for all that talent to go to waste.

choices.text: Okay, okay... Paimon is the best guide I could ever hope for.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. That's more like it.

choices.text: And no one's ever gonna separate us.
She even makes a pretty good travel guide...
You want a multifunctional robot for domestic application... Better known as Ineffa.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Northern Intelligence Network

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Northern Intelligence Network... What a mysterious-sounding organization!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A secret society, quietly pulling the strings behind the scenes, running the entire world from the shadows!

choices.text: "Secret society" seems like a stretch.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Ohh yeah, we do! Hey, this could be our foot in the door! We should totally join, then we can get one of those cool codenames! Like... ummm... Ooh, White Gold!

choices.text: Oh, because you have white hair and I have blond hair...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, yeah! This is our own nickname! The weird ones are reserved for other people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, don't the Knights of Favonius work with the intelligence network? What do you think Varka's codename is? "Grand Master"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, it's kind of hard to imagine Grand Master Varka doing spy stuff, isn't it? He's not exactly a low-key kinda guy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He'd probably go busting into the enemy base through the front gates, mowing down all the minions in his path, and then strut his way out with a briefcase full of intel in hand.

choices.text: ...I suspect that, as Grand Master,

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, good point! ...Wait, you're right, this isn't a secret society at all! More like a... who's-who of... people we know already!

choices.text: he probably delegates that kind of work to people like Kaeya and Rosaria.
An unusually sensible nickname, for once.
We know a whole bunch of the people involved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Strange Technology

choices.text: Come to think of it, we've met not one but two genius inventors in Nod-Krai, haven't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. And the proof of their genius is in the hi-tech pudding: Ineffa Pudding and Pulonia Pudding!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually... Okay, well "Pulonia Pudding" kinda works, Paimon's not gonna lose any sleep over that one... but Ineffa Pudding feels a little disrespectful...

choices.text: I'm speechless... After years of giving people ugly nicknames, you're finally learning!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey!

choices.text: Seriously though...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you for real!? Who's the name-caller now, huh!? Also, fantasizing about violence is a way worse habit than giving people ugly nicknames...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Honestly, though? After everything that's happened recently, it's hard to imagine them getting into a fight. Everyone's getting along pretty well these days.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just as dumb as trying to imagine Jean and Diluc in a fight...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can't believe you still remember that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ahem, but anyway... we're getting sidetracked. Back to Ineffa and Pulonia: I've thought of a foolproof way of figuring out who's stronger...

choices.text: All you'd have to do is lock them both in a room...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the...!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...And whoever gets destroyed last is clearly the strongest!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm, Paimon's not convinced. Like, sometimes, the more advanced technology is also the more fragile, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Ugh, what are we talking about? Enough! No more imaginary fights between friends!

choices.text: Then drop Lynette inside...
Who do you think would win in a fight between Ineffa the Annihilator and Pulonia the Pulverizer?
Yes, Paimon, name-calling IS disrespectful!
First Aino, and then Sandrone.
